title: How to write Etsy product descriptions with AI as your shop grows
summary: Learn how to write Etsy product descriptions with AI that stay warm and accurate as your team, catalog, and listing volume grow.
body_markdown:
Writing Etsy product descriptions gets harder once a shop stops being a one-person operation. When three people share the listing work, when a new collection lands in 12 colorways, or when a vintage restock adds 60 one-of-a-kind pieces in a week, descriptions can become the slow part of getting a product live.


Product photography has already sped up. In[Photoroom's April 2026 survey](https://www.photoroom.com/industry-trends/product-photography-cost-for-smbs) of 1,356 paying subscribers, the median time to a finished product image fell from about 15 minutes to under 5, and 36% of sellers said they spend the time they save listing more products. More listings means more descriptions to write, and each one is another chance for the shop's voice, the product facts or the variation details to slip.


An Etsy product description generator can take on the writing, as long as it doesn't flatten what makes each listing distinct.[Photoroom's Product Description Generator](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/product-description-generator) works from the product details you give it. Enter the product name and key facts, select Etsy as the marketplace, and it produces a warm, story-led description written for Etsy buyers, following Etsy's formatting, character limits and content rules.


This guide explains how to separate your shop's story from each product's facts, what an Etsy product brief should include, how to[create and review descriptions with Photoroom's Product Description Generator](https://www.photoroom.com/blog/how-to-write-product-descriptions-that-sell-online) , and how to keep the process consistent across a team.


## Table of Contents


## Why Etsy product descriptions get harder to write as your shop grows


[Etsy recommends](https://www.etsy.com/seller-handbook/article/1347574487014) sellers use their product description to relay important product information and tell a story about the product and brand. That's easy to deliver across ten listings. When that grows to three hundred listings, written by multiple people, a few common errors occur:


-


**The shop story gets cloned.** A paragraph about your studio or sourcing is pasted into every listing until it no longer says anything about the item the buyer is looking at.


-


**Warmth crowds out facts.** A description can sound personal and still leave out the skein weight, the dye lot or whether the chain is included.


-


**Options drift between listings.** Etsy listings can hold several sizes, colors or set quantities. Copy a description from a similar listing and the wrong options come with it.


-


**Disclosure becomes inconsistent.** One team member notes that hand-dyed colors vary between batches; another forgets. A buyer who wasn’t told has reason to feel that the item wasn’t as described.


None of these are really writing problems. They're information problems: the facts for each product aren't recorded anywhere reliable, so whoever writes the next listing starts from the last one.


## How to separate your Etsy shop story from your product facts


Keeping product details and product and brand story separate is how you scale product description generation across a catalog. Think of each description as containing three layers:


Layer What it holds How often it changes Example (hand-dyed yarn)


Shop layer Voice, how you make or source things, standard wording for care, variation and personalization Rarely We dye every skein by hand, in small batches.


Product layer Name, materials, weight, dimensions, quantity, listing options, what's included, verified care Per product 100 g skein, fingering weight, \[verified fiber blend\], colorway Harbor


Item story The detail of the making or sourcing that explains this particular item Per product Harbor is dyed in two passes, so the second color pools into darker speckles.


The shop layer belongs in one saved brand voice and a set of standard phrases, so it reads the same no matter who generates the description.


The product layer and item story belong in the details you enter for each product.


That third layer (the item story) is what keeps a story-led description honest and accurate. “Dyed in two passes” tells a buyer why their skein of yarn will have speckles and why it won't match the photo exactly.


A line about the shop's passion for color tells them nothing they can act on, and it’s the exact type of sentence that ends up getting copied and pasted into every listing.


## What should an Etsy product brief include?


A product brief is the record of what's true about one product. It's what you paste into the generator, what a teammate checks the draft against, and what you update when something changes.


For Etsy, a product brief should contain fields specific to the platform, like personalization and item story.


Field What to record Example (hand-dyed yarn)


Variation What differs between units and why Speckle placement and depth vary between skeins and between dye lots


Listing options What the buyer selects in this listing Single skein or set of 3 from one dye lot; colorways Harbor, Moss, Ember


Personalization What can be customized, and how to request it None for this listing


Included / not included Exactly what ships Yarn only; the pattern and needles shown in photos are not included


Buyer hesitation The question most likely to stop a purchase Whether skeins from separate orders will match for a larger project


Care Verified instructions Hand wash or machine wash cool on a gentle or wool cycle. Lay flat to dry.


Claims to leave out Appealing but unsupported statements “Colorfast” (not tested); “organic” (not certified); “exactly as pictured” (dye results vary)


Certain listing types require you to pay more attention to certain rows:


-


**For handmade pieces:** focus on materials, construction, physical qualities, personalization, care, and natural variation.


-


**For vintage pieces:** condition, repairs and item history replace the item story and natural variation rows. Anything you can't confirm, such as the decade or the fiber, should be recorded as unknown rather than guessed.


-


**For craft supplies:** quantity and compatibility matter more since the buyer may be checking whether the supply will work for a project they’ve already planned.


Keep the briefs somewhere the whole team can reach, such as a shared spreadsheet or your product catalog. Because you paste the details into the Product Description Generator and paste the finished result into Etsy, the brief is also your only record of what went into each description.


## How to create an Etsy product description with Photoroom’s Product Description Generator


[Photoroom's Product Description Generator](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/product-description-generator) is built for product listings rather than general writing, so there's no prompt to write and no need to explain what an Etsy description should look like. You fill in a few fields.


###


### 1. Add the product name and details


Paste the product layer and the item story from your brief. Include the natural variation note and the buyer hesitation you want answered, since the generator can only work with what you give it. Add the claims to leave out as a plain instruction.


For the yarn, the input might be:


Hand-dyed fingering weight yarn, colorway Harbor. 100 g skein, superwash merino, 400–465 yd. Dyed by hand in two passes; the second color pools into darker speckles, so speckle placement varies between skeins and dye lots. Sold as a single skein or a set of 3 from the same dye lot. Pattern and needles not included. Buyers often ask whether separate orders will match, so recommend buying all skeins for one project together. Do not describe as colorfast, organic, or exactly as pictured.


### 2. Set your brand voice and length


This is where the shop layer goes. Voice instruction should be specific enough to act on. For example:


Warm and plain-spoken, written as “we.” Mention the dyeing process only when it explains the yarn. Never use “made with love” or “perfect gift.”


If several people generate descriptions for the shop, create consistency by agreeing on one voice and have everyone use it.[Product Description Generator](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/product-description-generator) allows you to choose a preset voice from a list of options.


For length, a single-colorway supply with clear photos can be short. A listing with several options, a matching question to answer, or vintage condition to disclose is likely to need medium or long. You can choose one from the Product Description Generator’s dropdown menu.


### 3. Select Etsy


Choose Etsy as the marketplace. Photoroom shapes the copy for Etsy, applying its formatting conventions, character limits and content rules so you don't need to track them yourself. If you also sell the product on your own[Shopify store](https://www.photoroom.com/blog/shopify-product-descriptions-how-to-write-and-scale-better-copy) , or on[Amazon](https://www.photoroom.com/blog/how-to-write-an-amazon-product-description-with-AI) or eBay, select that marketplace and generate again from the same details. The structure changes for each channel. The facts don't.


### 4. Generate, review and paste


Generate the description and treat it as a first draft. The generator writes the description only, so your listing title, tags and attributes still come from you. Once the draft passes review, copy it into the description field of your Etsy listing.


## How to review an AI-generated Etsy product description


The most useful review habit for a growing shop is also the simplest: check every draft against its own brief, never against another description. That keeps an error in one listing from becoming the template for the next twenty.


For Etsy, ask:


-


**Is the story about this item?** If a sentence could sit in any listing in your shop, cut it or replace it with the item story.


-


**Can a buyer find the facts quickly?** Weight, dimensions, quantity and what's included shouldn't be hidden inside the third paragraph of prose.


-


**Is variation disclosed in your standard wording?** Hand-made variation should be described the same way across every listing in the shop.


-


**Do the options match the listing?** Every size, color or set mentioned in the description should exist in the listing, and the reverse.


-


**Are personalization instructions complete?** Buyers should know what they can customize and how to tell you.


-


**Has anything appeared that isn't in the brief?** Remove any material, certification or care claim you can't trace back to a verified fact.


-


**Do the photos agree?** If a styled image shows props, the description should indicate they’re not included.


When something is wrong, decide where the fix belongs. One clumsy sentence is quicker to correct by hand. A problem that appears in every draft, such as a missing dye-lot note, means the input is missing something. Add it to the brief and regenerate, and every description generated from that brief afterwards starts with the fix.


## How to use product photos to support your Etsy description


On Etsy, photos can show variation more clearly than a single sentence can. For example, a business selling handmade serving boards can make “grain and color vary” concrete for shoppers by showing three different boards side-by-side.


Before adding another paragraph, check whether an image would answer the question better:


-


If the silhouette is unclear, improve the image rather than writing another paragraph describing the shape.


-


If texture matters, show it closely and use the description to explain the verified physical feel or material.


-


If scale matters, provide a visual reference and exact measurements.


-


If a vintage product has a flaw, photograph it and explain it clearly in the description.


Photoroom can handle the production side of those images:[remove backgrounds](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/background-remover) for a clean primary image,[stage products in a lifestyle scene](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/product-staging) ,[add realistic shadows](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/instant-shadows) , and edit a whole new collection at once with[batch processing](https://www.photoroom.com/batch) .


One caution for handmade sellers: edited or generated images still have to show the real product. Only generate images if you have an existing product to reference it against, and check each visual against the actual product before uploading.


## How to review your Etsy listing before publishing: a checklist


Review your product description alongside the entire product listing: photos, options, titles and tags. Shoppers see all of these on the same page, so a description that passed review can still contradict a photo or an option added later. Run through it for every new listing, every new colorway or option, and every listing you update after a product changes.


### The description


-


The opening identifies the item. The first line names the product and the detail that sets it apart before any story begins.


-


The story is about this product. The item story explains something a buyer can see or use and isn't a general paragraph about the shop.


-


The facts match the brief. Weight, dimensions, quantity, materials and care are identical to the verified values, with nothing rounded, reworded into a stronger claim, or added by the generator.


-


Nothing from the claims-to-leave-out row appears. Check for reworded versions too.


### Options, variation and personalization


-


Every option in the description exists in the listing.


-


Variation is disclosed in your standard wording.


-


Personalization instructions are complete. Buyers know what they can customize, any limits, and how to send their details.


-


Vintage condition is fully disclosed. Every flaw, repair or unknown, such as era or fiber content, is stated rather than left for the buyer to discover.


### The photos and description together


-


Colors and finishes match the copy.


-


Styled props are accounted for.


-


Scale is consistent across images and the description.


-


Every image shows the real product. Edited or generated images reflect the actual item.


### The rest of the listing


-


Title, tags and attributes agree with the description. These are written separately from the generated description, so check they use the same product name, materials and options.


-


Nothing is carried over from another listing. If the listing started as a copy of an existing one, every field has been updated, not just the description.


If a check fails because of a one-off wording issue, fix it in the listing. If it fails because a fact was missing or wrong, correct the brief first and regenerate, so the next listing built from it doesn't repeat the mistake.


Etsy's requirements and search guidance change over time, so check for anything platform-specific before you publish.
